language.script_notes: Bavarian dialect appears informally. Blue-and-white Bavarian rhombus flag/livery visible on official signage and buildings in Bavaria specifically.

road_furniture.guardrail_type: More common on Alpine mountain roads.

architecture.roof_style: Steep-pitched roofs designed to shed Alpine snow; wide overhanging eaves on chalet-style buildings in the far south.
architecture.roof_material: Terracotta tile widespread; wood shingle on traditional Alpine buildings.
architecture.wall_construction: Half-timbered (Fachwerk) houses common in old towns (Baden-Württemberg, Franconia), often with decorative painted façades (Lüftlmalerei) especially in Bavaria; Alpine chalet-style timber construction in the far south near the Austrian border.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Warm pastel and white-painted half-timbered façades with dark wood beams; vividly painted Lüftlmalerei murals on Bavarian house fronts.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Onion-domed Baroque churches, a strong Bavaria/Austria-region tell; half-timbered Franconian and Black Forest old towns; Alpine chalets in Oberammergau/Berchtesgaden; Neuschwanstein-style fairy-tale castles.

nature.vegetation: Dense coniferous forest in the Black Forest and Bavarian Forest; farmland and orchards in the rolling foothills; alpine meadow at higher elevation.
nature.terrain: Rolling hills and forest rising sharply into the Alps along the southern border with Austria — the only part of Germany with true high-mountain scenery (Zugspitze, Germany's highest peak); the Danube River flows through.
nature.climate_signature: Snow-capped Alpine peaks visible on the southern horizon in many shots — a strong south-Germany-only tell; otherwise temperate and green.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Heavier concentration of premium German brands (BMW is Bavarian, Mercedes/Porsche headquartered in Baden-Württemberg's Stuttgart) than the national average.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 4, very dense around Munich and Stuttgart.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense urban and Alpine road coverage.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Near-identical Alpine architecture, onion-domed churches, half-timbered houses, shared dialect roots
confusion_set.tiebreaker: German plates carry a district-letter code distinct from Austrian district codes; this remains one of the genuinely hardest GeoGuessr pairs and often comes down to plate detail or road-sign fonts rather than architecture alone.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same script, plate and bollard style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The south has Alpine peaks, onion-domed churches and Lüftlmalerei-painted half-timbered houses; the north is flat with brick Gothic architecture and a low coastal horizon.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Alpine terrain and chalet-style architecture near the border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Swiss plates are white with a black canton code, no blue EU strip; German plates carry the blue 'D' EU strip.
